title: Validate Metal flash-attention tail padding
reason: Correctness-only Metal validation is complete: the old padding oracle has 8 passing controls and 12 byte mismatches; the fix passes all 20 cases. Both builds separately pass all 24 normal FA cases against the CPU reference. Performance, ASR and Vulkan remain unmeasured.
prior_evidence_note: Supplement outside the 34-measure speed ledger. No latency, CER or gain is assigned, and no campaign baseline is changed.

conditions.hardware_scope: Pre-M5 Metal; tensor API unavailable/disabled and shared Metal buffers enabled.
conditions.latency_definition: Latency is not measured. The four authorized hardware test executions are correctness checks, each run once, not timed worker requests.
conditions.aggregation: Report case counts and actual exit codes separately for old/new padding bytes and old/new CPU-reference attention checks. Do not combine these with request-latency or recognition-quality measurements.
limitations: This correctness supplement is outside the 34 optimization measures and contributes no speed-up or cumulative gain to the ledger.
Synthetic padding bytes and normal attention outputs are separate oracles. Old padding mismatches do not establish a runtime fault, wrong attention output, or an ASR recognition error.
Normal FA regression inputs randomize independently in each process. Passing the CPU reference on both builds does not establish cross-binary bitwise numerical equality.
No model weights, real speech, official model-stage dumps, ASR text, CER, latency, throughput, load time or memory were evaluated. The generic CER definitions below are not used for this supplement.
Windows/Vulkan and other Apple GPUs remain unverified. This is correctness-only M2 Ultra evidence, not whole-model validation or release acceptance.
The initial sandbox attempt ended before any cases because Metal was unavailable. It is retained separately and excluded from the old-build defect evidence.

The initial start timestamp and configure-old start/end timestamps are missing because the original date executable path did not exist. Empty captures remain unchanged; configure-old exit 0 and logs are intact.
CI for the parent change is not verified in this report. Hardware checks recorded here do not substitute for CI or Vulkan execution.
conditions.test_input_identity: Deterministic synthetic padding arrays with spare valid source storage; independently randomized normal FA arrays per process. Test-source hashes identify definitions, not recorded tensor bytes.

implementation_checkpoint.change: Copy logical K/V row bytes and zero the remaining destination pitch. Source strides, destination pitches, masks, attention arithmetic and quantized conversion are unchanged.
implementation_checkpoint.binary_paths_relative_to: outputs/haas-mac-flash-tail-pad-20261107 in the repository holding the local artifacts.

diagnostics.title: Padding-byte oracle: 20 cases on each build
diagnostics.method: Two types (F32/F16) x two query counts (1/20) x five shape/layout groups. Valid deterministic arrays include spare source storage; no fault-provoking input is used.
notes: All 20 case identities agree between old and fixed runs. All mask mismatch counts are zero on both builds.
The old build fails the padding/scratch-byte contract in the 12 named cases. Attention numerical outputs and recognition quality are not inferred from those failures.

diagnostics.title: Independent normal FA CPU-reference regressions
diagnostics.method: Each process runs the same 24 selected test definitions against its own CPU reference, with independently randomized inputs. Error thresholds are unchanged.
notes: There are zero unsupported or skipped selected cases. BLAS/CPU backend selection messages do not mean the Metal cases skipped their CPU reference.
LLAMA_TEST_FA_VEC_DISABLE=1 suppresses an unrelated extra slice that ignores the parameter filter; it is recorded on both sides.
Both vector and non-vector pre-M5 paths are covered by the fixture query counts. These results do not establish cross-binary bitwise equality.

diagnostics.title: Build and executable identity
diagnostics.method: Both standalone ggml builds use the same recorded Release/Metal/native configuration and -j4. These are test executables, not a speech worker or a production latency pair.
notes: A read-only import audit verified all 4 saved executables and 27 listed log files (30,434,155 bytes) against their original SHA-256 records. No model or audio file was read.
